constraints.title: Padding boundary
constraints.rule: The GCD of the gaps between distinct ciphertext lengths is the padding boundary, and it must equal the suite's max(block, 4).

constraints.title: Length residue
constraints.rule: Every ciphertext length satisfies len mod boundary == (IV + ICV) mod boundary; at least 90% must agree.

constraints.title: Minimum size
constraints.rule: The shortest ciphertext must hold the suite's IV and ICV plus 4 bytes of padding, pad length and next header.

constraints.title: Payload entropy
constraints.rule: Encrypting suites need mean entropy of at least 6.8 bits/byte; ESP-NULL must not exceed 7.2.

classes.name: AEAD or counter mode
classes.why_inseparable: All 4 members use an 8-byte IV, a 16-byte ICV and a 4-byte padding boundary, so the same plaintext produces the same ciphertext length under each of them. They differ only in the keyed transform, which never appears on the wire, so no length-based test can separate them.

findings.title: No quantum-resistant key establishment
findings.detail: The SA relies entirely on classical Diffie-Hellman. Traffic recorded today can be decrypted once a cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer exists, which matters for material whose sensitivity outlives the hardware.
findings.remediation: Deploy an RFC 8784 post-quantum pre-shared key now, and enable a hybrid ML-KEM key exchange (Group 35-37) as gateway firmware allows.

throughput.note: Capture too small to measure throughput: 742 packets, fewer than the 10,000 needed for a stable rate. Run `cipherguard bench` for a reproducible figure.

assumptions.note: The CRQC arrival estimate is a planning assumption, not a prediction. Substitute the agency's own figure; the ranking of links is unchanged by it, only the urgency framing.

links.rationale: ECP key exchange at 128 classical bits and zero quantum bits. Every session key on this link is recoverable by Shor's algorithm from recorded traffic.

phases.action: Enable hybrid key establishment: ML-KEM alongside the existing elliptic-curve group under RFC 9370, so the link stays secure if either primitive fails.
